records.subagent_summary: Execution 148.135 scored 1 of 8. Five rollouts hit the 16384-token cap with no boxed answer, oscillating between the two readings of the public value instead of carrying either to a conclusion; the two terminating failures picked the reading they had just argued was impossible and boxed a value from it. The one success carried a single reading through to the end. The incumbent says to enumerate interpretations but never says to finish one before opening another, nor which one to keep, so the student thrashes. This adds those two moves in place of the 'do not reason from the original set' clause only 2 of 8 rollouts echoed, and comes in shorter than the incumbent (75 vs 77 tokens). Branch discipline and a survivor-based test for choosing among readings help any multi-case problem.

Fresh rollouts (execution_id 148.136) scored 7/8. The one miss never formed a locus equation at all: it substituted individual roots, compared their moduli one at a time, found them unequal, declared the locus an ellipse 28 times over 13948 tokens, and boxed a guess. All seven passing traces instead did the same concrete thing the incumbent only gestures at with 'characterize the locus geometrically': parametrize, eliminate the angle to one x,y quadratic, divide by the common x^2,y^2 coefficient, complete the square. That vague branch is the clause the failing trace could not execute, so this edit names the executable route instead, at 69 tokens versus the incumbent's 70. Rounds 2 and 4 showed appending guards for this stall loses, and round 6 showed removing the concrete w=(z-1)/z anchor loses, so both are preserved.

Fresh rollouts scored 4/8. One never closed its reasoning block; two closed at 96-98 percent of budget and were truncated part-way through a long multi-section write-up before reaching any box; one failed on method, asserting the small figure lay wholly inside the large one by comparing center-to-side distances (32 such mentions) and boxing the containment value. The incumbent's setup clause is the weak link: 'extent' appeared 0-3 times per trace and its bare prohibition 'do not assume one figure sits inside another' did not stop that containment error. This edit replaces that vague gesture with one executable test - list the corners, decide containment by plugging corners into inequalities rather than comparing sizes - which is checkable on any placement/overlap problem. Round 6 showed rewording the output protocol costs held-out, so the protocol text is left untouched and the tail is trimmed to hold total length at the incumbent's 169 tokens.

Fresh round-7 rollouts (execution 148.138) scored 5/8. All three failures collapse to one factor because they believe a high-degree polynomial cannot agree with the affine target on several inputs without being linear: one caps a block at a single input and reports the menu size, one shrinks the cap by one, and one abandons the affine target entirely for finite differences of consecutive terms. The incumbent's closing clause only vaguely says to make each polynomial 'match L on its own block', giving no way to see that is possible. The edit spends those words on the explicit witness P=L+c(x-x_1)...(x-x_k), which visibly keeps degree deg P while equalling L on the whole block, and is one token shorter than the incumbent (152 vs 153).

Three of eight rollouts scored; four of the five failures ended in finish_reason=length. Each failure pinned the constants and set up the right single-unknown equation, then dropped a sign while expanding the cross-multiplied product, got no real roots, and spent the rest of the budget re-litigating the setup and the problem's validity instead of re-expanding that one algebraic line. The one correct rollout that hit the same dead end simply re-expanded the line, found the sign error and finished; another stopped early with a coordinate it never rechecked on the curve. The incumbent's 'relabel, not restart' clause is inert - no rollout ever relabels - so it is replaced by the concrete recovery move (re-expand the suspect line, then verify each surviving value) at identical length.

Fresh rollouts scored 2/8, the best in this hint's history, and the surviving failure is uniform: part (b) is priced without ever building the opening moves. Four rollouts answered a bare 1/n or 1/4 from an equally-likely-permutation claim, and two declared the placement impossible; several also read 'bottom' as arrived last rather than arrived first. No rollout in this or the prior round ever ran the incumbent's sum-to-one branch check, so that clause is inert transfer tax. This edit spends those tokens instead on the concrete first move the student lacks (push until the wanted item tops the buffer, then pop it, event settled) and capitalises FIRST, not last, to block the direction error. Net result is shorter than the incumbent, 184 vs 185 tokens, with no clause the successful rollouts relied on removed.

Fresh round-7 rollouts under the incumbent scored 0/8: six hit the 16384-token generation cap with no boxed value, and every rollout built the polynomial-in-x / Vandermonde model first, only mentioning a smaller case 8k-40k characters in. Two diagnostics: the phrase 'set the huge parameter to 2' is systematically misread (one trace read it as setting the coefficients to 2,3,4) because the hint never says WHICH quantity shrinks, and the divide-consecutive-entries/ratio clause is inert - 'ratio' appears exactly once (the quotation itself) in six traces and zero times in another. This edit names the shrink target concretely (number of unknowns) and swaps the ignored ratio clause for a single executable extraction step (one formula in n fitting every entry, signs included) plus an explicit box, at 69 tokens versus the incumbent's 70.

Fresh round-7 rollouts scored 5/8. Every one of the eight derived the gcd of the stage totals and listed its divisors as candidate counts, so that machinery works; all three failures then substituted the stated grouping count itself as the item count, calling it a reasonable assumption. The incumbent's clause 'it constrains the unknown count without being it' is an abstract negative that no rollout ever acted on, while the single rollout that applied the grouping count as a divisibility filter on the candidate list answered correctly. This edit replaces that inert clause with the same idea stated as one executable operation on a list the student has already written down, adding no tiebreak rule and no prohibition (both of which cost held-out in rounds 2, 4 and 6) and holding length at the incumbent's 123 tokens.

4/8 correct. All four failures ran to the 16384-token cap with nothing boxed, and two of them had already reached correct values before dying: they obeyed the incumbent's closing 'verify the identity at one numeric input' and spent the whole remaining budget evaluating the degree-9 composition with huge numbers. The other two acted on the same clause's 'test a different symmetry' licence and thrashed between restarts and full multinomial coefficient matching. No winning rollout ever ran a numeric verification; each read the values off the relation and stopped. So this keeps the involution ansatz wording the winners echo verbatim and swaps only that harmful trailing clause for the positive first move it lacked: treat a leftover free parameter as expected and commit a boxed answer as soon as it cancels. Net 8 tokens shorter.

Fresh rollouts under the incumbent scored 1/8, and six of eight died at the completion cap with one shared shape: the student did carry out the literal run and got counts, then a cycle-structure/disjoint-transposition argument contradicted those counts, and it spent thousands of tokens asking where the contradiction was instead of proceeding; the one finished failure overrode its own simulation with an invented cycle-order story. The lone success simply counted at small sizes and committed. So the missing instruction is a tie-break rule, not another prohibition: I replace the incumbent's pass-versus-pass convention clause and its bare 'a composite does not inherit the period of its parts' line (which rollouts recite verbatim and then ignore) with an explicit rule that the written-out states beat any structural argument, so keep the count and move on. Kept operation-agnostic and 8 tokens shorter than the incumbent.
